personality_traits: Anxious pre-emptive peacekeeper - opens the scene with a warning ('Be nice tonight') before anything has gone wrong
Passive and resigned rather than confrontational - reacts to his partner's confession with slack-jawed dismay instead of arguing back
Socially conflict-avoidant, clearly dreads his partner's bluntness in front of other guests
emotional_range: flat, heavy-lidded resignation while sipping his drink (0:03-0:06)
open-mouthed, wordless disbelief/horror as she reveals what she actually said (0:06-0:09)
expressions: droopy, half-closed eyes and a downturned neutral mouth from his first line 'Be nice tonight' (0:00)
eyebrows raised slightly, mouth slack as he delivers the accusation 'You told his last girlfriend...' (0:03)
jaw drops fully open, eyes still tired/hooded - a silent, deflated 'oh no' take as she doubles down (0:06-0:09), no dialogue but held on-screen reacting
gestures: holds a whiskey/rocks glass close to his chest the entire scene, never sets it down
stands rigidly upright behind the kitchen island, body barely moving - all reaction is facial
no hand gestures accompany his lines; stillness itself reads as suppressed anxiety
characters.interactions_notes: He initiates the exchange looking directly at her, establishing him as the one setting the social ground rules; once she answers, he does not look away, maintaining a fixed stare that ends in a dropped-jaw reaction shot with no comeback line, ceding the rest of the scene to her. Power dynamic: he sets expectations, she ignores them completely and escalates, leaving him mute and reactive - the classic straight-man role.

personality_traits: Blithely unapologetic - insists 'I'm always nice' immediately after being warned, showing zero self-awareness
Petty and score-keeping - reframes an obviously cruel remark ('her energy was a lot') as a selfless favor
Indignant that her rudeness wasn't appreciated ('She didn't even thank me'), revealing she genuinely believes she was in the right
Deadpan delivery masking casual cruelty - the humor comes from her calm, matter-of-fact tone about something clearly mean
emotional_range: unbothered, almost proud satisfaction recounting 'I did her a favor' (0:06)
genuine, petty indignation on 'She didn't even thank me' (0:08) - the emotional peak, played as real grievance rather than a joke to her
expressions: heavy-lidded, sly half-smile as she answers 'I'm always nice' (0:01-0:02), suggesting she knows exactly what she's about to reveal
mouth opens into a small 'o' of remembered pride as she recalls the comment (0:06)
eyebrows knit slightly, mouth downturned in genuine offense by 0:08's 'She didn't even thank me'
gestures: wine glass held at chest height throughout, small sip motions punctuating her lines rather than emphatic hand gestures
head tilts back slightly and eyes roll upward/sideways toward her partner when delivering the 'favor' line - a classic self-satisfied gesture
stands angled toward her partner the whole time, engaged and unbothered by his growing alarm
characters.interactions_notes: She never breaks eye contact or physical closeness with her partner despite his mounting horror, treating the conversation as normal small talk; her casual body language (sipping wine, faint smirk) contrasts sharply with his frozen, wide-mouthed reaction, and that mismatch is the joke. She holds conversational control for the entire scene - he asks/warns, she answers and escalates, and he never regains the floor.
